issues.legal_issue: A landholder who acquires land after commencement of a land-ceiling law and thereby exceeds the permissible area cannot reduce the surplus area by making later transfers or obtaining decrees diminishing the holding.
material_facts: In one appeal, a landholder who had held less than the permissible area inherited land and thereby came to hold more than that area; he later made a gift and possessory mortgages that reduced the land shown in his name.
In the other appeal, a landholder inherited additional land that took his holding above the permissible area and later transferred land to close relatives pursuant to a civil court decree.
The Collector disregarded the later transactions and declared surplus land; the High Court held that the transactions were not affected by the statutory scheme.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed. The later transfers and decrees could not be used to diminish the surplus area, and the surplus determinations were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 19B(1) and 19B(4) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, a person whose post-commencement acquisition takes the aggregate holding above the permissible area must declare the holding and the excess is available for the statutory surplus pool. Section 10A(c) requires relevant later judgments, decrees, or orders diminishing the area that could be declared surplus to be ignored. Section 10A(b)'s inheritance-related saving does not displace section 19B where the heir's aggregate holding itself exceeds the permissible area. The provisions should be interpreted to advance the Act's general purpose of building a surplus pool for redistribution, as held in Amar Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1974 SC 994, 996.

predicates.surplus_area_determination_proceeding: An authority is determining the surplus land of a person under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.post_commencement_acquisition_exceeds_ce: A person acquires land after the scheme begins and, together with land already held, exceeds the permitted holding.
predicates.later_disposition_or_decree_reduces_hold: After acquiring the excess, the person transfers land or obtains a decree that reduces the holding shown in the person's name.
predicates.later_dispositions_do_not_reduce_surplus: Later transfers or decrees are not counted to reduce the person's surplus area.

issues.definition: When a surplus-area determination follows a post-commencement acquisition that takes a person over the ceiling, a later transaction or decree reducing the person's apparent holding does not reduce the surplus area.

issues.legal_issue: The period allowed to declare land acquired in excess of the permissible area does not authorize transfers intended to defeat the land-ceiling scheme.
material_facts: The landholders were required, after acquiring holdings above the permissible area, to provide a return and select the land they wished to retain within a prescribed period.
The landholders made transfers during the period in which they could provide that return and make that selection.
The High Court treated the time allowed for filing the return as permitting those transfers.
issues.conclusion: The time allowed is a procedural facility for identifying inherited assets, selecting the land to retain, and filing the return; it cannot be used as an opportunity to defeat the substantive ceiling and redistribution scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19B(1) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, provides time for a person whose aggregate holding exceeds the permissible area to furnish a return and select land to retain. That procedural period does not suspend the substantive obligation to make excess land available under section 19B(4), or permit transfers to thwart the Act's purpose. The Court relied on the interpretive approach in Amar Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1974 SC 994, 996, and referred to the judicial role in giving effect to legislation as described in Corocraft Ltd. v. Pan American Airways Inc., [1968] 3 W.L.R. 714, 732.

rule.if: surplus_area_determination_proceeding and inheritance_creates_excess_holding and return_period_available and transfer_during_return_period

predicates.surplus_area_determination_proceeding: An authority is determining the surplus land of a person under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.inheritance_creates_excess_holding: A person inherits land that, together with land already held, exceeds the permitted holding.
predicates.return_period_available: The person is allowed a period to identify the acquired assets, select the land to retain, and file a return.
predicates.transfer_during_return_period: The person transfers land during the period allowed for filing the return and making the selection.

issues.definition: Where inheritance creates an excess holding in a surplus-area proceeding, the period for filing a return does not authorize a transfer during that period to defeat the ceiling.
